extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys/agents and respondents in USPTO OED disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for an affidavit of resignation submitted to the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) and the consequences (exclusion, publication, and reinstatement presumptions) that follow when the Director approves the affidavit under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director determined Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation complies with § 11.27(a) and therefore approved it. The affidavit should address the required elements (see other entries: voluntariness, awareness of investigation, consent to exclusion, knowledge of relevant regulations and consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary consent / no coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: "His consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit must affirm that the practitioner's consent to resignation/exclusion is voluntary and not the product of coercion or duress; this is an explicit element recited in the affidavit and relied upon by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending investigation (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge awareness that, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the OED Director opened an investigation of allegations that he/she violated the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit typically identifies the OED file and summarizes the matters investigated (e.g., state disciplinary actions reported to the USPTO). The affidavit should show the practitioner knew an investigation was pending and what it concerned (e.g., disbarment on consent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional misconduct standard: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is professional misconduct for a registered practitioner to be publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State." (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director may conclude that a practitioner's state public discipline constitutes professional misconduct under § 11.804(h)(1); such an opinion forms a basis for disciplinary action and for accepting resignation on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences upon approval: exclusion on consent from practice
rubrics_metrics.description: If approved, the Respondent shall be excluded on consent from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval of the affidavit results in exclusion on consent. The order directs publication of the exclusion and sets expectations for compliance with post-exclusion regulatory obligations (see entries on publication and compliance with §§ 11.58/11.60).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's statutory and regulatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has authority to approve an affidavit of resignation and exclude a practitioner on consent pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All approvals and exclusions rest on these statutory and regulatory bases; practitioners and OED should cite these provisions when processing or challenging resignations/exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement presumptions under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: By consenting to exclusion, the respondent acknowledges that, if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (a) the facts regarding him in OED File No. are true, and (b) he could not have successfully defended himself against the allegations embodied in the opinion of the OED Director that he violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a binding admission (limited to reinstatement proceedings) recorded in the affidavit and relied on by the Director; applicants for reinstatement should understand these presumptions will apply unless the regulatory scheme is otherwise satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; and Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 governs duty to notify clients and protection of client interests upon suspension/exclusion; § 11.60 sets the procedures and standards for reinstatement. The order explicitly requires compliance with these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements for exclusion on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the supplied Notice of Exclusion on Consent text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order supplies a model notice (identifying the practitioner, registration number, summary of facts, the rule allegedly violated, and statutory/regulatory authority) and requires publication for public reading and official record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of resignation while an investigation is pending
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may voluntarily submit an affidavit of resignation at a time when a disciplinary investigation is pending, and the Director may accept that affidavit and order exclusion on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explains that the respondent submitted the affidavit while an OED investigation was pending (concerning state disbarment on consent) and that the Director may accept such a resignation without the respondent admitting the alleged violations (subject to reinstatement presumptions).
